args: Analyze bailout safety of zend_string_extend() in php-src/Zend/zend_string.h, especially the GC_REFCOUNT(s) > 1 branch, and recommend the minimal root-cause fix. Does moving GC_DELREF(s) until after zend_string_alloc() and memcpy preserve ownership semantics, including persistent strings? Are there analogous helper patterns in the tree?

The supplied ASan report crashes during request shutdown in zend_gc_delref after the script `<?for(;$i.=$i.=0;$$i++)?>`. The reported root cause is that concat_function() at php-src/Zend/zend_operators.c:1968 calls zend_string_extend() in-place while another zval owns the same string. In php-src/Zend/zend_string.h, the shared-string branch reportedly decrements the original string before allocating its replacement. If allocation enforces the PHP memory limit and invokes zend_bailout(), the caller never receives the replacement and still points to the original with one ownership reference incorrectly removed. I am considering allocation/copy first and only then decrementing the original, but want to confirm semantics and whether the decrement should happen after allocation only or after memcpy as well.
